sentences.text: 1 1. This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose LAC no. 41/ 2016 (Award No.
25/200506/DC(NW)) Rohtash & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2636 Bighas 18 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 38//7 min (012), 3 (006), 15/1 min (0 12), 15/2 (108), 8//7 (416), 9 (409), 12/2 (219), 14 (416) total area measuring 19 Bigha and 18 Biswas, having 1/4th share each situated in the revenue estate of Village K. S. Nagar (Patti Nithari),
Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to LAC no. 41/ 2016 (Award No. 25/2005 06/DC(NW)) Rohtash & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
6.

sentences.text:
Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :
i) The LAC has not adopted correct method of assessment of market value of the said land on imaginary basis and on the basis of a government police.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be assessed and determined strictly as provided by law U/s 23 and 24 of LA Act, 1894.
ii) The LAC has not considered the location, developments, existing utility and potentiality of the land.
The present physical and existing location, developments and the utility and potentiality of the land, in and around the land of the petitioners were Rohtash Ors.

2 not taken into account.
iii) The LAC has erred in not taking into consideration the future potentiality and the utility of the acquired land of the petitioners.

The impugned award is arbitrary,
malafide and detrimental to the interest of the petitioners i.e. farmers.

The land of the petitioners has an increasing trend as regard to the market value after fixation of the rates of the agricultural land in Delhi and such rates have been increased by more than ten times.
The land of the petitioners have a very high value and is very fertile and leveled LAC no. 41/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Rohtash & Ors.

Vs.
Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 without any kind of depression or defect.
The said land be used for industrial or commercial or residential use with little efforts.
iv) The land of the petitioners is adjacent to welldeveloped areas, colonies and village Abadi and hence has a great market value.

The land enjoys all type of facilities/ civic amenities like developed metalled roads, electricity,
hospitals, government schools, public schools, computer institutes, full fledged post office, health gym, modern panchayat ghar, and most frequently served by DTC and various other private transporters as NH10, DelhiFirozpur Railway Line and main DelhiKanjhawala road passes by the side of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari).
There are nationalised bank operating with well established hospital and fully developed markets in village Kirari Suleman Nagar.
Land is also surrounded by Ghevara Industrial Area, Savada Industrial Area, Mundka Industrial Area with several godowns which are adjacent to the said village.

Government has provided all civic amenities like roads, transportation, electricity, water connections, schools, hospitals, telecommunications, etc where the market value is more than Rs. 10,000/ per sq. yards.
Therefore, the price of the acquired land should have been assessed minimum @ Rs 10,000/ per sq. yards.
v) The LAC has not taken into consideration the relevant sale/purchase transactions of the land in village Kirari Suleman Nagar and in the adjoining villages itself.

LAC has not announced any compensation for he standing crop of the petitioners and besides LAC no. 41/ 2016 (Award No.
25/200506/DC(NW)) Rohtash & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 this, the petitioner were fully dependent upon their agricultural land which has been acquired and not the petitioners are left without any source of income.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the petition as framed, is not maintainable as the petitioner has failed to furnish any evidence in respect of th relief claimed in the present petition and as such merits dismissal.
The LAC has already assessed the market value of the land in question taking into consideration the prevailing market rates of the land at the time of notification under Section 4 of the LA Act.
The possession of land measuring 17 Bigha only has been taken by the LAC and handed over to the DDA on 13.10.2006 and as such DDA is the necessary party being beneficiary of the said land.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.
9.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were LAC no. 41/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Rohtash & Ors.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
11. It is stated that the possession of the said land has been taken over by the DDA on 13.10.2006.
Whereas, the possession of land bearing Khasra No. 38//7 (412), 3 (106), 15/1 (412), 15/2 (1 08) has not been taken by DDA till date.

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 21.

As per the revised memorandum forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No.
38//7 min, 15/1 Min, 3 Min and 15/2 min has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.

22. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
LAC no. 41/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Rohtash & Ors.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 (3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
